author: sonnet
label: c2-seed-sonnet-01
changes: Replaced the skeletal one-line-per-component sketch with a real diagram showing numbered steps for send, fan-out and reconnect, as the brief asked.
Added a component list defining every name (outbox, relay, bus, presence, inbox) so a reader new to the stack can follow it.
Made the ordering explicit: the Inbox entry is written before delivery is attempted, and the offset is committed only after delivery, which is what makes crashes safe.
Replaced terse note fragments with a state table showing where each piece of state lives and for how long.

Wrote a failure-by-failure section covering store failure, crash after commit, relay/bus outage, worker crash, ack timeout, missed heartbeat, gateway crash, push failure, inbox expiry, ordering and duplicates.
Fixed an inaccuracy in the diagram: the outbox row is marked published by the Relay after the bus accepts it, not by the worker. The worker commits its bus offset after delivery.
Stated the idempotency mechanism: a unique msg_id in the Store for sender retries, and an Inbox key of (user, msg_id) for worker replays.
Stated the fan-out size (at most 199 recipients) and that the sender is excluded.
Added a short glossary paragraph up front defining seq, msg_id, heartbeat, fan-out and recipients, so the document stands alone.

Fixed the diagram: the Relay's 'mark published' step was numbered 11 at the end of the worker loop, which implied the worker did it. It is now 5b beside the Relay, and step 11 is the worker committing its bus offset.
Dropped 'last seq per conversation' from reconnect step R1 and the flow text, since the Inbox is what determines what is sent and the value was never used.
Stated that the worker handles recipients concurrently and commits its offset after all are handled, so the 5 s ack wait does not add up across 199 recipients.
Moved 'gateway holds no durable state' into the Gateway component and described the heartbeat refreshing the Presence entry.
Made the retry failure wording consistent (a retry returns the original ack and seq) and clarified when a timed-out recipient may see a duplicate.
Minor wording tightening: 'redelivers' became 'receives the event again', 'synced' became 'sent', 'no / timeout' simplified.
Moved the delivery-guarantee and one-device-per-user definitions into the opening terms list, and turned the terms into a list so each is easy to find.
Said what an Inbox entry contains (msg_id, conversation id, seq, no body), which explains why reconnect must fetch bodies from the Message Store.
Stated that the outbox row and message are written together so either both exist or neither does, and that the Store enforces unique msg_id.
Fixed a gap: an ack timeout now explicitly leads to a push, in the diagram (marked 'then do 9b') and in the flow text.
Clarified the retry-after-crash case: the Store recognizes the msg_id, writes nothing new, and returns the original ack.
Reworded the store-write-failure case to say no message or outbox row exists.
Noted that a worker retry can also repeat a push, and that the Gateway-crash case expires that gateway's Presence entries.
Spelled out TTL and minor wording cleanups for readability.
